memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.” -Acts 26:19

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
Saul of Tarsus was not a casual sinner; he was a convinced religious man. He believed he was serving Jehovah, yet he hated Jesus. He was zealous, educated, wealthy, disciplined, and fearless, but misdirected.
He defended the Law of Moses, not knowing that the Lawgiver Himself stood before him. God did not destroy Saul; God waited for him. He saw not Saul’s violent hands, but his honest yet ignorant heart.
On the road to Damascus, heaven interrupted religion with revelation. Not a sermon, a Person spoke. “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?”
That moment shattered pride, blinded natural sight, and opened spiritual eyes.
The persecutor became a penitent. The arrogant Saul became the submissive Paul. Once zealous for religion, now burning for the cross. He gave his life to the One who gave His life for him.

Paul never looked back. He lived aggressively against sin and Satan, boldly for Christ and His Church. So much so that even demons testified:
“Jesus I know, and Paul I know.” This is not mere conversion, this is transformation by encounter.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “God does not need your ability; He needs your surrender.”- D. L. Moody

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, Interru ,pt our religion with revelation.
Crush our pride, purify our zeal, and turn our passion fully toward You. Make us obedient to the heavenly vision. May the God who met Saul on the road meet us in your journey, transform our vision,
and use our life for His glory. In Jesus’ mighty name, Amen.Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: God may not approve your actions, but He sees your heart. One encounter with Christ can turn your past into a testimony and your zeal into eternal impact.
